title: Video Chatting: The AAP Exception Before 18 Months
summary: The American Academy of Pediatrics’ (AAP) 2016 statement makes an exception for video chatting in its advice to avoid screen media before 18 months. The difference is that the call is a real, two-way social interaction (Grandma responds to the baby’s smile), not passive broadcasting. Even this should be short and with your presence, naming the person and encouraging the child to wave and coo. The screen here is a means of relationship, not a means of entertainment—this is the balance that protects the child’s developing brain.
try_this: This week: Arrange a short video call (two minutes) with a beloved relative, and sit beside your child. Name the person, wave your child’s hand, and comment on the relative’s responses. Notice: Did your child interact (smile/coo) or remain a spectator?
reflection_prompts: What difference did you notice between your child’s attention during an interactive video call and leaving them in front of a broadcast video?
How can you make every moment of screen time (no matter how little) a moment of connection rather than a moment of silence?
